title: FleetCentric research
subtitle: Route optimization and rerouting for FAST NUCES Karachi shuttles
question: Can good shuttle routes be planned, and re-planned when a road is blocked, within free-tier compute limits (512 MB RAM, 0.1 CPU)?
caveats: Students are synthetic (bus loads 65 to 90 percent of capacity), not real registrations.
Travel times are free-flow OSRM times with no traffic; real morning times are higher.
Rerouting scope for FYP-1: morning runs to campus only, one bus rerouted at a time.

items.title: Optimization
items.question: Can all-stop routes be built from a travel-time matrix within free-tier CPU and memory limits, and how do they compare with the current hand-made routes?

items.title: Rerouting
items.question: When a road is blocked, which road and which stops (keep, skip, or let students walk to a nearby point) give the lowest student delay, within the same limits?

items.title: Context
items.question: How much do real incidents slow shuttle routes, recorded on an H3 grid?

items.title: Prediction
items.question: Does that context predict travel times better than the timetable and the router?

planned_experiments.title: Road-block test
planned_experiments.question: Does OSRM really route around a road when its speed is set to 0, does a slowed road (not fully blocked) work too, and how long does re-customizing take?

planned_experiments.title: Walking-radius sweep
planned_experiments.question: For walking limits from 0 m (visit every stop) to 800 m, how many minutes does letting students walk to a nearby point save after a block? Run on the frozen closure scenarios, against the patched published route (simplest fix) and the no-time-limit oracle.

planned_experiments.title: Must-serve stops
planned_experiments.question: How many minutes do must-stop rules (accessibility, unsafe walking after dark) add to a reroute, on the same scenarios and baselines?

next_steps: Write the optimization chapter from LOGBOOK runs B1 and Q1. Standard search budget from now on: 300 s (60 s is the minimum).
Run the traffic check and the seed check from the hub (about 15 minutes together; rules fixed in LOGBOOK 2026-11-10) and add them to the chapter.
Freeze a set of road-closure scenarios on or near shuttle routes, including the Shahrah-e-Faisal protest closure and University Road flooding.
Fix the rerouting baselines and scores in the logbook before any run: patched published route, no-time-limit oracle; delay against the oracle, students asked to walk, extra walking distance.
Road-block test: set a road's speed to 0, and to a slow speed, in OSRM and time the re-customize (needs Docker).
Build the rerouting pieces: walking graph, covering-path solver, H3 corridor pruning. After a block, re-query only nearest-neighbour travel times and estimate the rest on the high side (run Q1).
For every new experiment: push the logbook entry with the pass/fail rule before the first run, and judge on the worst repeat as well as the median.
